causal-factors.rationale: Closing of the Verizon acquisition on January 20, 2026 eliminates Frontier as a standalone issuer and repays Frontier's debt, significantly reducing bankruptcy risk in the May 1, 2026 window, and Frontier's reported liquidity (~$2.3 billion) with no debt maturities before 2027 (as of June 30, 2025) supports a lower near-term bankruptcy risk ahead of closing (Globe Newswire turn1search0; Investing.com turn1search4; Frontier Q2 2025 results turn0search5).

synthesis: Accounting for the Verizon deal closing in early 2026, Frontier ceases to exist as an independent entity, eliminating meaningful bankruptcy risk before May 1, 2026. The liquidity cushion and lack of near-term maturities further reduce risk, implying a calibrated probability around 1% with a narrow range.
